title: The Weighing of the Heart
subtitle: Feather, scales, and the monster at the door — Egypt's afterlife entrance exam

narrativeBlocks.title: The Hall of Two Truths
narrativeBlocks.body: After death, you arrive at the hall where Osiris presides and your whole life is audited. This is the Judgment of the Dead — and it's not a vague reckoning; it is a literal test.

narrativeBlocks.title: The negative confession
narrativeBlocks.body: You recite a list of everything you did NOT do: 'I have not stolen, I have not killed, I have not lied, I have not made anyone hungry.' Forty-two declarations before forty-two judges.

narrativeBlocks.title: Heart against feather
narrativeBlocks.body: Then the scales: your heart is weighed against the feather of Maat — truth, order, the rightness of the cosmos. A heart light as the feather lives; a heart heavy with wrongdoing does not pass.

narrativeBlocks.title: The devourer at the scales
narrativeBlocks.body: Waiting beside the scales is Ammit — part crocodile, part lion, part hippo: 'the devourer of the dead.' If your heart fails the test, she eats it — and that is the second death, the true end.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why this picture lasts
narrativeBlocks.body: The Judgment scene is Egypt's most copied image — and the idea that a life is weighed is older than any courtroom. Egyptians carried cheat-sheet Book of the Dead scrolls to help their hearts pass.

quiz.prompt: What is weighed in the Judgment of the Dead?

choices.text: Your deeds against a stone tablet
Your heart against the feather of Maat — truth and right order
Your name against the king's list

quiz.explanation: The heart is the seat of conduct — it must be as light as truth itself.

quiz.prompt: What happens to a heart that fails the weighing?

choices.text: Ammit devours it — the second death, final annihilation
It is sent back to earth reborn
It serves Osiris in the fields

quiz.explanation: There's no hell-torment — just non-existence, delivered by a monster at the scales.
